headline: Load spike and mounting sleep debt — today's tempo stays on, but trimmed and gated on how the legs feel.
body_state: Readiness sits at 48 (moderate, overtraining status "caution"), and today's deterministic verdict is red: acute:chronic load ratio 1.83 (>1.5 carries 2–4× injury risk next week) on top of 25h of 14-day sleep debt after only 6.3h last night. Deep sleep was just 11% of that (target 13–23%) — the restorative stage got shortchanged. HRV held balanced at 48ms and body battery recharged +48 overnight, but sits at 46 now, with resting HR up to 50. Training is also monotonous (2.1; >2.0 flags overtraining risk) — too many similar-intensity days back to back.
session: Plan calls for 10min easy + 4km tempo @ 4:18–4:32/km + 10min cooldown. Given the load-spike flag, run it — but protect it: hold the slow edge of the tempo window (4:28–4:32/km) rather than chasing the fast end, and if the legs feel flat after 1–1.5km, cut the block short rather than forcing all 4km. This is exactly the session the readiness gate exists for: the aerobic stimulus survives a shorter or slower tempo, not a broken one. Skip Un1t or any other hard cross-training today — one hard stimulus, not two.
recent: Tue (8/11): a hard AM Un1t class (53% time in Z4, RPE 7, no cooldown — HR still climbing at the finish) paired with a genuinely easy 32km PM road ride (70%+ Z1–Z2, avg HR 106) — good pairing in principle, but stacking both in one day fed today's load spike. Mon (8/10): the "easy" 5km treadmill run actually ran moderate — 89.7% of it sat in HR zone 3 at 4:27/km, cadence still low at 157.6 spm. Sun (8/9): a clean easy 21km hilly ride, 90%+ Z1–Z2. The pattern repeating: cross-training rides come in properly easy, but the run days keep landing in the grey zone — exactly why it tops the limiter list again.
focus: Trim today's tempo to the slow edge of the pace band, or cut it short if legs feel flat — the load spike is real (ACWR 1.83).
Actually slow the easy days: HR 115–130, not 4:20s/km — this is the direct fix for the #1 limiter (grey-zone training).
Get to bed ~60min earlier this week — 25h of accumulated sleep debt is capping today's readiness.
